title: design(atlas): semi-automated ingestion operations — source set, usefulness filter, disk/IO + plan-spend guardrails

body:
Parent: [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018) (Atlas ingestion program). Statements S1–S5 of the 2026-11-04 brief.

## Requirement (Drew, in substance)

Atlas updates become **semi-automated on a long-term plan** — not ad-hoc manual ingestion runs. The automation:

1. **Ingests the operational source set automatically**: reboots / boot records, session logs, chat logs, statistics, and reports are added to Atlas as they are produced.
2. **Applies a usefulness filter**: data that is useless to have in Atlas is NOT uploaded. Semi-automated ≠ indiscriminate — every source class carries an inclusion test (what question would this ever answer?).
3. **Monitors disk and I/O**: ingestion watches storage consumption and I/O load on the source and target machines and throttles / pauses / reports rather than filling a disk or swamping a host.
4. **Never spends more than the plan**: the current paid plan is a hard ceiling (today: Turso scaler, $24.92/mo yearly). Design treats plan limits (storage, reads/writes, DB count) as the budget envelope; growth that would cross the plan is surfaced to Drew, not silently incurred. Cf. [#5468](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5468) (pm-stack mirror storage surge) for what unmonitored growth looks like.

## Current state

- Ingestion today is script-driven and manual (scripts migrating into code + fleet under [#5670](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5670)); staging tier with merge-on-close promotion exists ([#5669](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5669)).
- Sources produce data continuously (boot records in `~/logs/init.jsonl` + init-status; OpenCode session store; Muse chats; quota/statistical reports) but nothing sweeps them into Atlas on a cadence.
- Storage rulings (2026-11-04): Turso + D1 both used, Turso embedded replicas first-class, huge atlases shard across both, cold tiers → rustfs; TursoDB for all NEW databases; production atlas stays libSQL for now.

## Design must answer

- Trigger model per source class: scheduled sweep vs event-driven (file close, session end, boot completion) vs hybrid; what "semi" means — which steps stay human-approved (new source classes? classification changes? bulk backfills?).
- The usefulness test: per-class inclusion rules, who/what applies them (static allowlist, size/shape heuristics, classifier pass), and how a rejected class is logged (rejection is data — cf. S32's unassociated-log principle).
- Disk/IO guardrails: watermarks, backpressure behavior, where the monitors live (source host vs ingest host), interaction with the delta-only design (companion issue under [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018)) so sweeps stay cheap.
- Cost accounting: per-run and per-source ingest cost (storage delta, write volume) reported against plan headroom; alert before the ceiling, not after.
- Failure posture: a failed/partial sweep never corrupts or double-ingests (idempotent, content-addressed landing per [#3125](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3125)).

## Done looks like

A design doc (in code, `doc/`) + follow-on implementation issues: per-source trigger table, usefulness rules, guardrail thresholds, cost report format, and the runbook for the recurring sweeps. Implementation itself is follow-on work, not this issue.
